gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in the5krunner's four-person seated test against an Omron upper-arm cuff, the Huawei Watch D3 read low on 18 of 20 systolic readings and 16 of 20 diastolic readings. The per-person average gaps reached -14/-8 mmHg (139/90 on the cuff, 125/82 on the watch) and -13/-17 mmHg (115/76 on the cuff, 102/59 on the watch). Notebookcheck's three-reading test found the D3's mean systolic reading only 0.5% below an Omron RS4 wrist monitor's, but its diastolic reading about 11% higher.
standout_why: I compared against these cited rival pages: Hilo's comparison blog (us.hilo.com, no mmHg figures, only 'accuracy has been demonstrated via multiple clinical trials'), TechRadar's D3 launch story (the fetch returned only its headline, no figures), Android Authority's Samsung US rollout story (HTTP 403, could not open), Cardilog (TLS certificate error, could not open) and Wareable's D3 review (HTTP 403, could not open). A search summary says Wareable compared the D3 with an Omron M2 Essential over four consecutive readings that came out close (for example 119/73 vs 118/70), but I could not open the page to confirm this. If it holds, the cited rival tells the shopper the cuff watch matches a cuff. None of the pages I could read gives a multi-person comparison, the direction of the bias (consistently low), or a formal validation figure for the Omron HeartGuide.
decides: ChatGPT's second chat ranks the Huawei Watch D3 'Best for actual blood pressure measurements'. Named measurements partly support this: on systolic, Notebookcheck measured the D3's mean 0.5% below an Omron RS4. They also qualify it: the5krunner found the D3 read low on most readings across four people, with two people reading 13–17 mmHg low on one number. Only the Omron HeartGuide (HEM-6410T-ZM) has a published ISO 81060-2 validation with numbers: -0.9 ± 7.6 / -1.1 ± 6.1 mmHg (Kuwabara et al., 2019). For a shopper who wants readings they can act on, this favors the HeartGuide, or at least checking any cuff watch against an upper-arm cuff. The cuffless options are a different case. Notebookcheck's single pair for the Hilo Band was 5/8 mmHg high, and a 2026 Digital Health study found smartwatch errors grew to 3.4/5.1 mmHg once blood pressure moved 10 mmHg from the calibration point. Both point to using these bands for trends, not for spot readings.

findings.label: the5krunner four-person test vs an Omron upper-arm cuff (cuff → watch, mmHg, average of the middle 3 of 5 readings)
findings.value: S1 146/95 → 141/88 (-5/-7); S2 116/75 → 108/77 (-8/+2); S3 115/76 → 102/59 (-13/-17); S4 139/90 → 125/82 (-14/-8). Read low on 18 of 20 systolic and 16 of 20 diastolic readings; one diastolic reading was 27 below the cuff
findings.source_title: Huawei Watch D3 Review – Blood Pressure Watch 95% Accurate (the5krunner, tfk)
findings.note: Published 2026-09-24, updated 2026-10-29. Four people aged 55–65, seated, five cuff readings then five watch readings each; highest and lowest dropped, middle three averaged. The Omron model is not named; a second Omron cuff agreed with it 'within 2 points'. The headline '95%' comes from a separate one-person test (cuff 151/91, D3 147/84) and is the reviewer's own percent-of-reference metric, not a clinical standard. Mean of the four per-person gaps, my arithmetic: -10 systolic / -7.5 diastolic.

findings.label: Notebookcheck hands-on vs an Omron RS4 wrist monitor
findings.value: D3 mean systolic 0.5% below the Omron RS4; D3 diastolic about 11% above; runs averaged 118/74 mmHg
findings.source_title: Huawei Watch D3: Hands-on with medical-grade blood pressure monitoring and new features (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner)
findings.note: Published 2026-09-16. Three alternating readings on each device; posture and timing not stated. A second check against a Braun ExactFit 5 Connect upper-arm monitor is described only as 'even closer parity', with no figures. The page does not say whether 118/74 is the watch's average, the Omron's, or both.

findings.label: Lab validation to ANSI/AAMI/ISO 81060-2:2013, mean difference vs reference (SBP/DBP)
findings.value: Criterion 1: -0.9 ± 7.6 / -1.1 ± 6.1 mmHg; Criterion 2: -0.9 ± 6.8 / -1.1 ± 5.5 mmHg; passed both criteria
findings.source_title: Kuwabara M, Harada K, Hishiki Y, Kario K. Validation of two watch-type wearable blood pressure monitors according to the ANSI/AAMI/ISO81060-2:2013 guidelines: Omron HEM-6410T-ZM and HEM-6410T-ZL. J Clin Hypertens 2019;21(6):853-858 (Europe PMC record of PMID 30803128)
findings.note: Abstract figures, e-published 2019-02-25. The larger-wrist variant HEM-6410T-ZL: 2.4 ± 7.3 / 0.7 ± 7.0 mmHg (criterion 1). ISO pass thresholds are a mean of ≤5 mmHg and an SD of ≤8 mmHg. Participant count is not in the abstract.

findings.label: Notebookcheck single paired reading vs a Braun ExactFit 5 Connect upper-arm monitor
findings.value: Braun 125/79 mmHg vs Hilo Band 130/87 mmHg (+5/+8 mmHg); 21% battery left after two weeks
findings.source_title: Hilo Band review: Smart blood pressure tracker with medical certification (Notebookcheck, Daniel Schmidt)
findings.note: Published 2025-10-14, page shows an update of 2026-11-01. Only one pair, taken through the band's calibration function because readings can't be triggered manually. The band was tested, not the US Hilo Core bundle.

findings.label: Long-term smartwatch BP vs an Omron M4 cuff over 28 days, mean difference
findings.value: SBP -0.34 mmHg, DBP 0.62 mmHg overall; rose to 3.4 mmHg (SBP) and 5.1 mmHg (DBP) when reference BP was 10 mmHg from the calibration point
findings.source_title: Walzel S, Sebestova H, Rafl-Huttova V, Rozanek M, Rafl J. Long-term accuracy and stability of blood pressure measurements from a smartwatch: Prospective validation study. Digital Health 2026;12 (PMID 41602947)
findings.note: Published online 2026-01-22, 37 participants. Europe PMC returned it for a query requiring 'Galaxy Watch', but the abstract text I read did not name the watch model, so don't attribute it to a specific Samsung model on the page until the paper is opened. SDs not given in the abstract. The authors advise cuff confirmation when BP shifts substantially.

unsourced: Wareable's Huawei Watch D3 paired readings vs an Omron M2 Essential (a cited rival): the page returned HTTP 403, so I could not confirm the pairs (e.g. 119/73 vs 118/70) shown in a search summary.
